Fort Collins Water-Demand Data Audit

Acquisition, validation, coverage, and modeling-readiness review

Author

Colin Furey

Published

August 3, 2026

Purpose

This report audits the data used in the municipal water-demand forecasting project before model development. It verifies provenance and integrity, summarizes temporal and variable coverage, examines basic distributions and relationships, and records limitations that should guide downstream feature engineering and evaluation.

The audit is generated from committed repository artifacts rather than from manually entered summary values. Re-rendering this document after the data pipeline changes will update its tables and figures automatically.

Executive summary

TipReadiness determination

The validated and processed data are suitable for exploratory analysis and time-series model development. The only saved warning concerns the optional NOAA wind variable (AWND), which has incomplete raw coverage and is excluded from the initial processed dataset.

Data provenance and lineage

The processed table is built only after the raw snapshots pass the saved cross-source validation report. Each raw and processed file is accompanied by metadata containing its retrieval or generation time, row count, schema, and SHA-256 checksum.

Join integrity

Schema and modeling roles

The primary modeling target is water_demand_mgd. The City’s projected demand, the actual-to-projected ratio, and plant demand are retained for auditing and context but are not default predictors. Their availability at a genuine forecast origin would need to be established before they could be used as features.

Coverage and completeness

Daily calendar coverage

The final year is a partial year ending March 31, 2026. Annual comparisons must therefore avoid treating 2026 as a complete calendar year.

Raw NOAA variable coverage

AWND is preserved in the raw NOAA snapshot but excluded from the processed table because its 83.26% coverage would introduce missingness into the first analysis-ready dataset. No wind imputation is performed at this stage.

Weather characteristics

Temperature and demand

The correlations above are exploratory associations, not estimates of causal weather effects. Seasonality, trends, repeated observations, and delayed responses can influence the values.

City projection reference fields

The source contains both observed and City-projected demand. The project keeps the projected series as a reference for understanding the source data, but it is not included among the default forecasting predictors.

Deterministic transformation checks

The processed builder creates several deterministic fields. This report rechecks their identities rather than assuming they were generated correctly.

Modeling-readiness considerations

WarningTime-series leakage

Random train/test splits are not appropriate for the primary evaluation. Validation should preserve chronological order through a fixed holdout, rolling-origin evaluation, or another explicitly time-aware design.

The following decisions should carry into model development:

  1. Target. Use water_demand_mgd as the initial outcome. Continue treating the City projection, observed/projected ratio, and plant demand as reference columns unless their real-time availability and intended interpretation are established.

  2. Weather variables. The first processed table uses complete temperature, precipitation, snowfall, and snow-depth fields. AWND remains available in raw data but is excluded rather than silently imputed.

  3. Calendar variables. Integer month and weekday encodings are convenient audit fields, but some models may need categorical or cyclical representations instead of assuming a linear numeric effect.

  4. Lagged demand features. Lags and rolling summaries can be useful, but every feature must be computed using only information available before the prediction date. Rolling calculations should be shifted before model fitting.

  5. Partial final year. The series ends March 31, 2026. Full-year summaries and year-over-year comparisons must account for the incomplete 2026 period.

  6. Single weather station. The primary station provides complete core coverage, but one station cannot represent every microclimate within the utility service area. This is an explicit scope limitation of the minimum viable analysis.

  7. Source status. The water-demand data are preserved as a dated raw snapshot because the City’s open-data platform was undergoing migration. Future refreshes should be compared against the current snapshot and accompanied by updated acquisition metadata.

Audit conclusion

The data pipeline produces a complete one-to-one daily table with verified provenance, matching checksums, no duplicate dates, no missing calendar dates, and no missing processed values. The dataset is approved for the next stage: time-aware exploratory forecasting baselines and feature engineering.

The audit should be re-rendered whenever raw snapshots, source endpoints, station choices, processing rules, or processed outputs change.
